chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor narrated together, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor, from his father, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu al-Jarud, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Hamdani, from al-Harith al-A'war al-Hamdani, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (Ali) said from the pulpit: 'When the Ill-wisher perishes, the Master of the Age disappears, and hearts remain fluctuating—some fertile and some barren—then the Ill-wishers will perish, the vanishers will vanish, and the believers will remain, and they will be few, three hundred or a little more. A group that fought with the Messenger of Allah on the day of Badr, who were neither killed nor died, will fight with them.'

key_terms.الْخَاطِبُ: The Ill-wisher (referring to the enemy of the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْمُتَمَنُّونَ: The Ill-wishers (those who wish for the delay of the Imam's arrival)
key_terms.الْمُضْمَحِلُّونَ: The vanishers (those who fade away or disappear)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْعَصْرِ: The Master of the Age (referring to the Mahdi)
key_terms.عِصَابَةٌ: A group (specifically referring to the angels of Badr)
key_terms.يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ: The day of Badr (the first major battle in Islam)

ai.seo_question: Who are the three hundred believers that will fight with the Imam of the Age?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ali (as) describes the eschatological state of the 'Minor Occultation' period, where societal instability leads to the purification of the faithful into a small, steadfast remnant of approximately three hundred. This group is uniquely supported by the angels who fought at Badr, symbolizing divine assistance during the era of waiting (*Intizar*) before the reappearance of the Imam of the Age.
